title: Global minimum variance weights from a return panel
deliverables: summary json: portfolio vol (annualised), sum of weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N] decimal per period, periods per year P. DITANYAKAN: GMV weights [N] (fractions, sum 1), annualised portfolio vol (decimal). RUMUS: Core 1: w=S^-1 1/(1'S^-1 1); sigma_p=sqrt(w'Sw P); S sample cov ddof=1. JAWAB: 1) sort dates, fix asset order. 2) S=np.cov(R.T, ddof=1) [N x N]. 3) x=solve(S,1). 4) w=x/sum x. 5) vol=sqrt(w'Sw)*sqrt(P). 6) check sum w=1, S symmetric PD; write.
pitfalls: using inv() on near-singular S instead of solve; mixing ddof=0 and ddof=1

title: GMV and portfolio stats from given mu and Sigma
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N] already annual (or stated frequency). DITANYAKAN: GMV weights [N], expected return w'mu and vol sqrt(w'Sw) in the given frequency. RUMUS: Core 1 GMV; A=1'S^-1 1, B=1'S^-1 mu; E[r_gmv]=B/A, var=1/A. JAWAB: 1) verify Sigma symmetric; build from vols and correlation if given as sigma_i, rho_ij: S=D C D. 2) solve S x=1. 3) w=x/A. 4) report w'mu, sqrt(w'Sw). 5) check E=B/A, var=1/A.

title: Tangency (max Sharpe) portfolio with a risk-free rate
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N] or returns [T x N]; rf (annual or per period); Sigma [N x N]. DITANYAKAN: tangency weights [N] summing to 1, its expected return, vol, Sharpe (annualised). RUMUS: Core 1: w=S^-1(mu-rf)/1'S^-1(mu-rf); SR=(w'mu-rf)/sqrt(w'Sw)=sqrt((mu-rf)'S^-1(mu-rf)). JAWAB: 1) put mu, rf, S in one frequency (rf/P simple). 2) x=solve(S, mu-rf). 3) w=x/sum x (if sum<0, tangency is on the lower branch - report sign). 4) stats. 5) annualise mean x P, vol x sqrt(P), SR x sqrt(P). 6) check SR equals sqrt formula.
pitfalls: normalising when 1'S^-1(mu-rf) < 0 flips the portfolio; rf frequency mismatch

title: Mean-variance utility optimum for risk aversion delta
deliverables: weights [N] (may not sum to 1; residual in cash)
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N] (excess of rf if stated), Sigma [N x N], delta scalar. DITANYAKAN: w*=(1/delta)S^-1 mu [N], cash 1-sum w, utility w'mu-(delta/2)w'Sw. RUMUS: Core 1 MV utility; with budget constraint use Lagrange w=(1/d)S^-1(mu-g1), g=(1'S^-1mu-d)/(1'S^-1 1). JAWAB: 1) decide excess vs raw mu from text. 2) w=solve(S,mu)/delta. 3) if fully invested required, apply Lagrange gamma. 4) utility and certainty equivalent. 5) check gradient mu-delta S w = 0 (or = gamma 1).

title: Minimum-variance portfolio for a target return (frontier point)
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N], target m (same frequency). DITANYAKAN: weights [N] with w'mu=m, sum w=1 minimizing variance; frontier vol at m. RUMUS: A=1'S^-1 1, B=1'S^-1 mu, C=mu'S^-1 mu, D=AC-B^2; w=[(C-Bm)S^-1 1+(Am-B)S^-1 mu]/D; var=(Am^2-2Bm+C)/D. JAWAB: 1) compute S^-1 1, S^-1 mu via solve. 2) A,B,C,D. 3) w for m. 4) check w'mu=m, sum w=1, var formula equals w'Sw. 5) efficient if m>=B/A.

title: Efficient frontier table over a grid of target returns
deliverables: table per target [G]: target, vol, weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N], grid of G targets or count G between min and max mu; long-only flag. DITANYAKAN: per grid point [G]: min vol and weights [N]. RUMUS: Unconstrained: closed form (A,B,C,D). Long-only: QP min w'Sw s.t. w'mu=m, 1'w=1, w>=0 (SLSQP or cvxpy). JAWAB: 1) grid from min to max of feasible mu (long-only: [min mu_i, max mu_i]). 2) per m solve QP from a feasible start (equal weights). 3) clip tiny negatives, renormalise only if within tolerance. 4) table sorted by target; check vol non-decreasing above GMV.
formulas: min w'S w s.t. w'mu = m, 1'w = 1, w >= 0
long-only target range [min mu_i, max mu_i]
pitfalls: infeasible targets outside asset mean range in long-only case

title: Long-only minimum variance with weight bounds
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma [N x N] (or returns), bounds lo<=w_i<=hi, budget 1. DITANYAKAN: constrained GMV weights [N], vol, which bounds bind. RUMUS: QP: min w'Sw s.t. 1'w=1, lo<=w<=hi; KKT: (Sw)_i equal for interior names. JAWAB: 1) S from returns ddof=1. 2) start equal weights. 3) scipy minimize SLSQP with tight ftol, jac 2Sw. 4) check feasibility sum=1, bounds; KKT: marginal risk equal on interior assets, higher on names at lower bound. 5) annualise vol.
formulas: min w'S w, 1'w = 1, lo <= w <= hi
KKT: (S w)_i = lambda for lo < w_i < hi

title: Long-only maximum Sharpe portfolio
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N], rf, long-only and optional cap. DITANYAKAN: weights [N] maximizing (w'mu-rf)/sqrt(w'Sw) with w>=0, sum 1. RUMUS: Convex reformulation: min y'Sy s.t. (mu-rf)'y=1, y>=0; w=y/sum y. Or SLSQP on -SR. JAWAB: 1) excess mu. 2) if all excess <=0, no positive-SR portfolio - report per text. 3) solve QP for y. 4) w=y/sum y. 5) report SR annualised sqrt(P). 6) check SR >= SR of every single asset.
formulas: min y'S y s.t. (mu - rf)'y = 1, y >= 0; w = y/1'y
pitfalls: the y-trick is invalid with an upper cap on w; use direct SLSQP then

title: Shrinkage covariance (Ledoit-Wolf) before optimisation
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]; target (identity scaled, constant correlation) or fixed intensity d. DITANYAKAN: S_shrunk=d F+(1-d) S [N x N], GMV weights from it, intensity d. RUMUS: Ledoit-Wolf: d*=max(0,min(1,kappa/T)) with kappa=(pi-rho)/gamma; constant-correlation F_ij=rbar sqrt(s_ii s_jj). JAWAB: 1) demean returns, S (state ddof; sklearn LedoitWolf uses 1/T). 2) target F. 3) intensity: given d or LW estimate. 4) S_sh. 5) GMV via solve. 6) check S_sh PD, diag unchanged for const-corr target.
formulas: F_ij = rbar sqrt(s_ii s_jj), F_ii = s_ii
sklearn LedoitWolf target mu_bar I, mu_bar = trace(S)/N
pitfalls: sklearn LedoitWolf uses MLE 1/T covariance, not ddof=1

title: Risk contribution table of given weights
deliverables: per-asset table [N]: weight, marginal, contribution, percent
frame: DIKETAHUI: weights [N], Sigma [N x N] or returns [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: MRC_i=(Sw)_i/sigma_p, RC_i=w_i MRC_i, pct_i=RC_i/sigma_p; sigma_p. RUMUS: Core 2 Euler decomposition; toolkit component_var (measure var) for VaR version. JAWAB: 1) align weight order with Sigma columns. 2) Sw [N]. 3) sigma_p=sqrt(w'Sw). 4) MRC, RC, pct. 5) annualise sigma and RC by sqrt(P) consistently. 6) check sum RC = sigma_p, sum pct = 1.

title: Equal risk contribution (ERC) risk parity weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N] or Sigma [N x N]. DITANYAKAN: ERC weights [N] (sum 1, positive) with equal RC_i, and RC table. RUMUS: Core 2: Spinu convex min 0.5y'Sy - sum b_i ln y_i, b_i=1/N; w=y/sum y. Gradient Sy - b/y = 0. JAWAB: 1) S ddof=1. 2) start y=1/sigma_i. 3) Newton or scipy minimize (L-BFGS-B, y>0) to tol 1e-12. 4) w=y/sum y. 5) RC_i; check max|RC_i - sigma_p/N|<1e-8. 6) write weights and RCs.
formulas: min_y 0.5 y'S y - sum b_i ln y_i, y > 0
ERC condition w_i (S w)_i = w'S w / N
pitfalls: stopping at loose tolerance; equal weights are not ERC unless S has equal vols and correlations

title: Risk budgeting with unequal budgets
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma [N x N], budgets b [N] (sum 1, positive). DITANYAKAN: weights [N] with RC_i/sigma_p = b_i. RUMUS: Spinu with budgets b: min 0.5y'Sy - sum b_i ln y_i; w=y/sum y. JAWAB: 1) normalise b to sum 1. 2) solve convex problem. 3) w. 4) pct RC_i=w_i(Sw)_i/w'Sw. 5) check |pct-b|<1e-8.
formulas: min 0.5 y'S y - b' ln y

title: Inverse-volatility weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]; lookback window W; rebalance schedule. DITANYAKAN: w_i=(1/sigma_i)/sum(1/sigma_j) per date, realized portfolio returns. RUMUS: Core 2 inverse-vol; sigma_i = std of trailing W returns (ddof=1), data strictly before rebalance date. JAWAB: 1) per rebalance date use rows t-W..t-1. 2) sigma_i. 3) weights. 4) apply from next period; drift between rebalances. 5) portfolio returns [T]; annual stats. 6) check sum w=1 each date.
pitfalls: using the current-period return in the vol window (look-ahead)

title: Inverse-vol versus ERC comparison and equal-correlation check
deliverables: table [N]: w_ivol, w_erc, RC under each
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma [N x N] (or vols [N] and correlation [N x N]). DITANYAKAN: both weight vectors, RC tables, whether they coincide. RUMUS: Inverse-vol equals ERC iff all pairwise correlations equal (Maillard-Roncalli-Teiletche). JAWAB: 1) ivol weights. 2) ERC via Spinu. 3) RCs for each. 4) gap max|w_ivol-w_erc|. 5) check: set correlation to constant rbar and confirm gap ~0.
formulas: ERC with constant rho: w_i proportional to 1/sigma_i

title: Equal-weight (1/N) rebalanced portfolio with drifting weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N] simple; rebalance frequency. DITANYAKAN: rebalanced vs buy-and-hold return series, turnover per rebalance. RUMUS: Drift w_i'=w_i(1+r_i)/sum w_j(1+r_j); turnover=sum|w_target-w_drifted| (one-way = half). JAWAB: 1) w0=1/N. 2) each period r_p=w'r. 3) drift weights. 4) at rebalance, turnover vs target, reset. 5) buy-and-hold = no reset. 6) annualise; check wealth = cumprod(1+r_p).

title: Black-Litterman implied equilibrium returns (reverse optimisation)
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma [N x N]; market caps or w_mkt [N]; delta or market excess return and variance. DITANYAKAN: Pi=delta S w_mkt [N] (excess returns, same frequency as S). RUMUS: Core 3 and 5: Pi=delta S w_mkt (no tau); delta=(E[r_m]-rf)/sigma_m^2. JAWAB: 1) w_mkt=cap/sum cap. 2) delta given or from market data. 3) Pi=delta S w. 4) check w_mkt recovered: (delta S)^-1 Pi = w_mkt.
pitfalls: multiplying tau into Pi

title: Black-Litterman posterior with absolute views
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma [N x N], Pi [N] (or w_mkt, delta), views: asset k returns Q_k; tau; Omega or rule. DITANYAKAN: P [V x N] one-hot rows, mu_BL [N], weights. RUMUS: Core 3: mu_BL=[(tS)^-1+P'O^-1P]^-1[(tS)^-1 Pi+P'O^-1 Q]; Core 4 default O=diag(P tS P'). JAWAB: 1) build P rows (1 in asset column). 2) Q [V]. 3) Omega per rule (variance). 4) M=inv((tS)^-1+P'O^-1P). 5) mu_BL=M[(tS)^-1Pi+P'O^-1Q]. 6) weights per text. 7) check each mu_BL between prior and view direction.
formulas: mu_BL = M [(tau S)^-1 Pi + P' Omega^-1 Q]

title: Black-Litterman relative view (outperformance spread)
deliverables: summary: view-implied spread before and after
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma, Pi, view: asset A outperforms B by Q (or basket vs basket with market-cap weights), tau. DITANYAKAN: P row (+1 A, -1 B or cap-weighted legs), posterior returns, weights. RUMUS: Core 3; equivalent form mu_BL=Pi+tSP'(PtSP'+O)^-1(Q-P Pi). JAWAB: 1) P row sums to 0 for relative views. 2) basket legs: weights within leg proportional to cap (Idzorek) or equal per text. 3) O diag(P tS P'). 4) mu_BL via update form. 5) check P mu_BL lies between P Pi and Q.
formulas: mu_BL = Pi + tau S P'(P tau S P' + Omega)^-1 (Q - P Pi)

title: Black-Litterman with Idzorek confidence levels
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma, Pi, P [V x N], Q [V], confidences c_k in (0,1], tau. DITANYAKAN: omega_k, posterior mu_BL, weights. RUMUS: Core 4: omega_k=((1-c_k)/c_k) p_k tS p_k'; c=1 -> omega 0, use limit mu satisfies view exactly. JAWAB: 1) omega_k per formula. 2) if any c_k=1, use update form with O having zeros (P tS P' + O stays invertible). 3) mu_BL=Pi+tSP'(PtSP'+O)^-1(Q-PPi). 4) weights. 5) check: c->0 gives Pi, c=1 gives P mu_BL=Q.
formulas: omega_k = ((1 - c_k)/c_k) p_k tau S p_k'
pitfalls: inverting Omega with a zero entry; use the update form

title: Black-Litterman with view uncertainty given as std
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma, Pi, P, Q, view std s_k (or confidence interval half-width), tau. DITANYAKAN: Omega=diag(s_k^2), mu_BL, posterior covariance. RUMUS: Core 4: omega_k=s_k^2 (variance, not std); interval +-h at z -> s=h/z. JAWAB: 1) convert stated std to variance in S frequency (annual std -> daily var s^2/P). 2) Omega diagonal. 3) BL update. 4) posterior S_post=S+M. 5) check smaller s pulls harder toward Q.
pitfalls: using s instead of s^2

title: Black-Litterman optimal weights with posterior covariance
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma, w_mkt, delta, tau, P, Q, Omega. DITANYAKAN: w_BL=(delta S_post)^-1 mu_BL with S_post=S+M (or (delta S)^-1 mu_BL per text), tilts. RUMUS: Core 3: S_post=S+M; He-Litterman w=w_mkt/(1+tau)+P'Lambda form. JAWAB: 1) Pi=delta S w_mkt. 2) M, mu_BL. 3) S_post=S+M. 4) w=solve(delta S_post, mu_BL). 5) tilt. 6) check: no views gives w_mkt/(1+tau) under S_post, w_mkt under S.
formulas: no views: w = w_mkt/(1+tau) with S_post
pitfalls: choosing S vs S_post silently; follow text

title: Black-Litterman no-view sanity check
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma, w_mkt, delta, tau; empty view set. DITANYAKAN: posterior equals prior; weights equal market weights. RUMUS: Core 3 with V=0: mu_BL=Pi. JAWAB: 1) Pi. 2) skip view terms (P empty). 3) mu_BL=Pi. 4) w=(delta S)^-1 Pi=w_mkt. 5) report residuals ~1e-12.

title: Risk aversion delta from market data for Black-Litterman
deliverables: summary: delta, market excess return, market variance
frame: DIKETAHUI: market returns [T] or market-weight returns of assets, rf. DITANYAKAN: delta=(E[r_m]-rf)/sigma_m^2 in one frequency. RUMUS: Core 5. JAWAB: 1) market return series r_m=w_mkt'R or index. 2) excess mean, variance ddof=1. 3) delta (frequency-invariant if mean and var share frequency). 4) use with Pi.
pitfalls: mixing annual premium with daily variance

title: Black-Litterman with annual views and daily covariance
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily returns [T x N], views Q annual, view stds annual, tau. DITANYAKAN: posterior returns in one consistent frequency. RUMUS: Card convention: keep BL in ONE frequency; daily Q=Q_ann/P, omega=s_ann^2/P (or /P^2 when stated as given in the card). JAWAB: 1) S daily ddof=1. 2) Pi daily. 3) convert Q and Omega to daily per text. 4) BL update. 5) annualise mu_BL x P for output. 6) check result equals running all-annual (S x P, Pi x P) inputs.
pitfalls: mixing annual views with daily S

title: Kelly fraction for a binary bet
frame: DIKETAHUI: win probability p, net odds b (win b per 1 staked), loss of stake on failure. DITANYAKAN: f*=p-q/b, growth g=p ln(1+fb)+q ln(1-f). RUMUS: Core 6 binary; toolkit kelly_fraction(p=, b=). JAWAB: 1) q=1-p. 2) f=p-q/b (=(bp-q)/b). 3) if f<=0, no bet. 4) g(f*). 5) check derivative pb/(1+fb)-q/(1-f)=0.
formulas: g(f) = p ln(1 + f b) + q ln(1 - f)
pitfalls: using gross odds instead of net odds

title: Continuous Kelly for one asset and its growth rate
deliverables: summary: f*, growth at f*, growth at half kelly
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu, sigma (annual) of risky asset, rf. DITANYAKAN: f*=(mu-r)/sigma^2, g(f)=r+f(mu-r)-f^2 sigma^2/2. RUMUS: Core 6; toolkit kelly_fraction(mu, sigma, rf). JAWAB: 1) excess mu-r. 2) f*. 3) g* = r + SR^2/2. 4) half Kelly g = r+3/8 SR^2. 5) report leverage f*.

title: Multi-asset Kelly vector
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N], rf. DITANYAKAN: f=S^-1(mu-r) [N], leverage, growth g. RUMUS: Core 6: f=S^-1(mu-r); g=r+f'(mu-r)-f'Sf/2. JAWAB: 1) same frequency. 2) f=solve(S,mu-r). 3) leverage=sum|f| (may exceed 1; do not normalise). 4) g. 5) check gradient (mu-r)-Sf=0.
formulas: g = r + f'(mu - r) - f'S f/2
pitfalls: normalising Kelly weights to sum 1

title: Fractional Kelly growth and volatility trade-off
deliverables: table per fraction [K]: fraction, growth, vol
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu, sigma (or vectors), rf, list of fractions c. DITANYAKAN: for each c: growth g(c f*), vol c sigma_f. RUMUS: toolkit fractional_kelly(f, fraction); g(c)=r+(c-c^2/2) SR^2. JAWAB: 1) f*. 2) per c, f_c=c f*. 3) g and vol. 4) check half Kelly keeps 3/4 of excess growth at half vol.

title: Kelly sizing capped by a VaR limit
deliverables: summary: s, VaR before and after
frame: DIKETAHUI: Kelly weights f [N] or scalar, mu, Sigma, confidence a, VaR limit VaR_max (positive loss). DITANYAKAN: scale s=min(1, VaR_max/VaR(f)), sized weights s f, VaR(s f). RUMUS: Core 7: VaR(w)=z_a sqrt(w'Sw)-w'mu (positive homogeneous); toolkit var_constrained_fraction. JAWAB: 1) Kelly f. 2) VaR(f) in horizon of the limit. 3) s. 4) s f. 5) check VaR(s f)=VaR_max when s<1; direction kept.
pitfalls: mean sign: raw vs excess mean in VaR - follow text

title: Parametric portfolio VaR and component VaR
deliverables: per asset [N]: marginal VaR, component VaR, pct
frame: DIKETAHUI: weights [N] or positions $, Sigma, mu (optional), confidence a, portfolio value V. DITANYAKAN: VaR_p, mVaR_i, cVaR_i summing to VaR_p. RUMUS: toolkit component_var(weights, cov, level, value, mu, measure='var'); mVaR_i=z (Sw)_i/sigma_p. JAWAB: 1) sigma_p. 2) VaR=V(z sigma_p - w'mu). 3) marginal z(Sw)_i/sigma_p - mu_i. 4) component w_i mVaR_i V. 5) check sum component = VaR_p.

title: Volatility targeting with ex-ante covariance and leverage cap
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N], base weights [N] or per date, target sigma_tgt (annual), window W, cap. DITANYAKAN: scale_t=min(cap, sigma_tgt/sigma_hat_t), scaled returns. RUMUS: Core 8: sigma_hat=sqrt(P w'S_trail w), full covariance from rows before t. JAWAB: 1) per t, S_trail from t-W..t-1. 2) sigma_hat annualised. 3) scale. 4) r_t=scale_t w'r_t (apply next period). 5) realised vol of scaled series; check scale<=cap.
pitfalls: diagonal covariance for a hedged long-short book

title: Volatility targeting with EWMA realised volatility
frame: DIKETAHUI: strategy returns [T], lambda (0.94 default), target, cap, seed variance rule. DITANYAKAN: EWMA vol series, lagged scale, scaled returns, realised stats. RUMUS: sigma_t^2=lambda sigma_{t-1}^2+(1-lambda) r_{t-1}^2; scale uses sigma known at t-1. JAWAB: 1) initialise variance (first-W sample var or r_0^2 per text). 2) recursion. 3) annualise sqrt(P). 4) scale_t=min(cap,tgt/sigma_t). 5) scaled r. 6) check no same-day return in its own scale.

title: Rebalanced strategy with transaction costs and net returns
deliverables: per period: gross, cost, net return [T]
summary: total turnover, annual net return
frame: DIKETAHUI: target weights per rebalance [R x N], returns [T x N], cost c bps per unit traded. DITANYAKAN: turnover per rebalance, cost, net return series. RUMUS: turnover=sum|w_new-w_drift|; cost=c/1e4 x turnover (two-way unless one-way stated). JAWAB: 1) drift weights between dates. 2) at rebalance compute traded. 3) net_t=gross_t-cost_t (on rebalance day). 4) first book from cash: turnover=sum|w|. 5) annualise; check net<=gross.
pitfalls: forgetting the initial build trade or using one-way when two-way is meant

title: Gaussian HMM Baum-Welch regime fitting
deliverables: params: mu [K], sigma [K], A [K x K], pi [K]
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T] (one series), K states, initial params, tolerance, max iterations. DITANYAKAN: fitted params, smoothed probs gamma [T x K], hard states, logL, iteration count. RUMUS: Core 9 log-space forward-backward, M-step MLE variances (no ddof). JAWAB: 1) log b_k(x_t) normal logpdf. 2) forward alpha, backward beta with logsumexp. 3) gamma, xi. 4) M-step mu, sigma^2, A over t<T-1, pi=g_0. 5) iterate until |dlogL|<tol. 6) final E-step with final params. 7) label bull=higher mean; check rows sum 1.
formulas: log alpha_t(k) = log b_k(x_t) + lse_j(log alpha_{t-1}(j) + log A_jk)
sigma_k^2 = sum gamma x(x - mu_k)^2 / sum gamma
pitfalls: probability-space underflow; labelling by state index instead of mean

title: HMM log-likelihood and filtered probabilities for given parameters
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T], mu [K], sigma [K], A, pi (fixed). DITANYAKAN: filtering P(s_t|x_1..t) [T x K], total logL. RUMUS: Core 9 forward recursion only; logL=lse_k log alpha_T(k). JAWAB: 1) log emissions. 2) forward pass log-space. 3) filtered=exp(alpha_t - lse alpha_t). 4) logL. 5) check rows sum 1; no future data in filtered probs.
formulas: P(s_t = k | x_1..t) = exp(log alpha_t(k) - lse_j log alpha_t(j))

title: Viterbi most likely regime path
deliverables: summary: path log-probability, counts per state
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T], HMM params mu, sigma, A, pi. DITANYAKAN: Viterbi path [T] and its log-probability. RUMUS: Core 9 Viterbi: delta_t(j)=max_i[delta_{t-1}(i)+log A_ij]+log b_j(x_t); backtrack argmax. JAWAB: 1) delta_0=log pi+log b(x_0). 2) recursion with argmax pointers. 3) last state argmax delta_T. 4) backtrack. 5) map state ids to bull/bear by mean. 6) compare with gamma>0.5 hard assignment if asked.
formulas: delta_t(j) = max_i [delta_{t-1}(i) + log A_ij] + log b_j(x_t)

title: Regime-conditional allocation using per-regime covariance
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N], regime labels [T] (from HMM), minimum days threshold, rule per regime. DITANYAKAN: per regime mu_k, S_k, weights; switching portfolio returns. RUMUS: Core 1-2 per regime; card: too few days -> full-sample covariance. JAWAB: 1) hard regime labels (lagged to avoid look-ahead). 2) per regime subset rows; if count < threshold, fall back. 3) weights (GMV/tangency/ERC per text). 4) apply weights of regime known at t-1 to returns at t. 5) stats.
pitfalls: using regime of day t to trade day t

title: Historical VaR and expected shortfall of a portfolio
deliverables: summary: VaR and ES (positive) per level
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N], weights [N], confidence levels a. DITANYAKAN: VaR=-q_{1-a}(r_p), ES=-mean(r_p | r_p<=q) (positive magnitudes). RUMUS: Core 10; toolkit portfolio_returns, var_from_portfolio, var_es_historical. JAWAB: 1) r_p=R w. 2) q=np.quantile(r_p,1-a) linear. 3) ES mean of returns <= q (or worst ceil((1-a)T) per text). 4) report positive. 5) check ES>=VaR, monotone in a.
pitfalls: sign convention: report losses as positive

title: Minimum CVaR portfolio by Rockafellar-Uryasev LP
frame: DIKETAHUI: scenario returns [S x N], confidence a, long-only budget, optional target return. DITANYAKAN: weights minimising CVaR, optimal z (VaR), CVaR value. RUMUS: Core 10: min z+1/((1-a)S) sum u_s, u_s>=-r_s'w - z, u_s>=0, 1'w=1, w>=0. JAWAB: 1) losses L_s=-r_s'w. 2) LP variables (w, z, u). 3) scipy linprog highs. 4) CVaR=objective. 5) check z ~ VaR of optimal loss distribution, CVaR>=z.
formulas: min z + (1/((1 - a) S)) sum_s u_s

title: Mean-CVaR efficient frontier
deliverables: table per target [G]: target, CVaR, weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: scenarios [S x N], a, grid of target means. DITANYAKAN: per target the min CVaR and weights. RUMUS: Core 10 LP plus constraint mean_s(r_s)'w >= m. JAWAB: 1) mean vector from scenarios. 2) for each target add constraint. 3) solve LP. 4) table; check CVaR non-decreasing in target.
formulas: min CVaR s.t. mu'w >= m, 1'w = 1, w >= 0

title: Monte Carlo wealth paths and drawdowns of competing allocations
deliverables: per strategy: mean, median terminal wealth, P(loss), median max drawdown
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N] (or bootstrap returns), strategies' weights, horizon H, paths M, seed, W0. DITANYAKAN: terminal wealth distribution and drawdown stats per strategy. RUMUS: Card: one seeded default_rng, one draw set shared; wealth=W0 cumprod(1+r); drawdown path includes W0. JAWAB: 1) rng=np.random.default_rng(seed). 2) draws [M x H x N] multivariate normal once. 3) per strategy r=draws@w. 4) wealth, running max including W0. 5) stats; toolkit max_drawdown per path.
pitfalls: re-drawing per strategy; omitting W0 from the drawdown path

title: Absorption ratio of the covariance matrix
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N], window W, number of eigenvectors k (often N/5). DITANYAKAN: AR_t = sum top-k eigenvalues / trace per window, standardised shift. RUMUS: Core 12; correlation trace=N. JAWAB: 1) rolling window rows t-W+1..t (label end date). 2) covariance or correlation per text. 3) eigvalsh descending. 4) AR. 5) shift=(AR_15d mean - AR_1y mean)/std per text. 6) check 0<AR<=1.

title: Random-matrix cleaning of a correlation matrix (Marchenko-Pastur)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: MP upper edge, number of signal eigenvalues, cleaned matrix, GMV from it. RUMUS: Core 12: lambda_+=(1+sqrt(N/T))^2; replace noise eigenvalues by their average, keep trace N. JAWAB: 1) standardise, correlation C. 2) eigen-decompose. 3) noise = lambda<=lambda_+. 4) set noise eigenvalues to their mean. 5) rebuild, rescale diag to 1. 6) S=D C D, GMV.

title: Brinson-Hood-Beebower single-period attribution
frame: DIKETAHUI: per sector: portfolio weight wp, benchmark weight wb, returns Rp_i, Rb_i (beginning weights). DITANYAKAN: BHB effects per sector, totals equal Rp-Rb. RUMUS: Core 11 BHB: alloc=(wp-wb)Rb_i, sel=wb(Rp_i-Rb_i), inter=(wp-wb)(Rp_i-Rb_i); toolkit brinson_attribution. JAWAB: 1) normalise weights per side. 2) Rp=sum wp Rp_i, Rb=sum wb Rb_i. 3) effects. 4) check sum effects = Rp-Rb exactly. 5) write in percent if asked.
pitfalls: end-of-period weights

title: Brinson-Fachler allocation relative to total benchmark
deliverables: per sector [S]: BF allocation, selection, interaction
frame: DIKETAHUI: same as BHB inputs. DITANYAKAN: BF allocation (wp-wb)(Rb_i-Rb) per sector; totals. RUMUS: Core 11 BF; sector values differ from BHB, totals equal since sum(wp-wb)=0. JAWAB: 1) Rb total. 2) alloc_i=(wp_i-wb_i)(Rb_i-Rb). 3) selection and interaction as BHB (or selection with wp if interaction merged). 4) check totals = Rp-Rb and equal BHB totals.

title: Brinson attribution with a cash sector
frame: DIKETAHUI: sector table plus portfolio cash weight, cash rate (annual). DITANYAKAN: effects with cash line (benchmark wb=0). RUMUS: Core 11; cash: wb=0, Rb_cash=Rp_cash=cash rate per period -> allocation only. JAWAB: 1) cash return per period (annual/12 monthly). 2) add cash row wb=0. 3) effects; cash selection=0. 4) check totals.

title: Multi-period Brinson attribution: sum vs geometric linking
frame: DIKETAHUI: monthly sector tables [T x S], linking method. DITANYAKAN: per period effects and cumulative linked effects matching compounded active return. RUMUS: Card default plain sum; toolkit link_attribution(period_frames, method='carino'). JAWAB: 1) per period BHB/BF. 2) plain sum unless linking asked. 3) Carino: k_t=ln(1+Rp_t)-ln(1+Rb_t) over (Rp_t-Rb_t), K overall; scale each effect by k_t/K. 4) check linked sum = prod(1+Rp)-prod(1+Rb).
pitfalls: benchmark weights drifting within a quarter when fixed is stated

title: Returns-based style analysis (Sharpe style weights)
frame: DIKETAHUI: fund returns [T], style index returns [T x K]. DITANYAKAN: nonnegative style weights summing 1 minimising tracking variance, R2. RUMUS: toolkit returns_based_attribution(port, factors, method); QP min var(r - F b) s.t. b>=0, 1'b=1. JAWAB: 1) align dates. 2) QP via SLSQP. 3) residual = selection return. 4) R2=1-var(e)/var(r). 5) check weights sum 1.

title: Maximum diversification portfolio
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma [N x N] (vols sigma [N]). DITANYAKAN: weights maximising DR=w'sigma/sqrt(w'Sw). RUMUS: Unconstrained: w proportional to S^-1 sigma; long-only via QP min y'Sy s.t. sigma'y=1, y>=0. JAWAB: 1) sigma=sqrt(diag S). 2) solve. 3) normalise. 4) DR. 5) check DR>=1 and >= DR of equal weights.

title: Minimum tracking error portfolio versus a benchmark
frame: DIKETAHUI: Sigma, benchmark weights b [N], allowed names subset, constraints. DITANYAKAN: weights minimising (w-b)'S(w-b), TE annualised. RUMUS: QP: min (w-b)'S(w-b) s.t. 1'w=1, w>=0, w_i=0 outside subset. JAWAB: 1) S. 2) solve QP. 3) TE=sqrt((w-b)'S(w-b) P). 4) IR if expected active return given.

title: Performance summary of an allocation backtest
deliverables: summary json: cagr, vol, sharpe, max drawdown, sortino, calmar
frame: DIKETAHUI: portfolio returns [T] decimal, P, rf per period. DITANYAKAN: standard stats. RUMUS: toolkit sharpe(returns, P, rf_per_period), cagr, annualized_vol, max_drawdown, performance_summary. JAWAB: 1) wealth cumprod. 2) CAGR=W_T^(P/T)-1. 3) vol std ddof=1 sqrt(P). 4) SR mean excess/std sqrt(P). 5) MDD from running max. 6) Sortino with downside dev; Calmar=CAGR/|MDD|.
formulas: Sortino = mean(r - rf) sqrt(P)/sqrt(mean(min(r - rf, 0)^2) P)

title: Normal expected shortfall and marginal ES of portfolio
frame: DIKETAHUI: weights, Sigma, mu, confidence a, value V. DITANYAKAN: ES=V(sigma_p phi(z)/(1-a) - w'mu), components. RUMUS: toolkit component_var(..., measure='es'); ES homogeneous degree 1 so Euler applies. JAWAB: 1) z=Phi^-1(a). 2) sigma_p. 3) ES. 4) component w_i[(Sw)_i phi(z)/((1-a)sigma_p) - mu_i]V. 5) check sum = ES >= VaR.
formulas: cES_i = w_i [(S w)_i phi(z_a)/((1 - a) sigma_p) - mu_i]

title: Dollar-neutral long-short mean-variance with gross constraint
deliverables: summary: net, gross, expected return, vol
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N], constraints 1'w=0, sum|w|<=G. DITANYAKAN: weights, net exposure 0, gross G. RUMUS: Unconstrained neutral: w proportional to S^-1(mu - g 1), g=(1'S^-1mu)/(1'S^-1 1); then scale sum|w|=G. JAWAB: 1) x=S^-1 mu, y=S^-1 1. 2) w=x-(1'x/1'y) y. 3) scale to gross G. 4) check 1'w=0 within 1e-12. 5) stats.
formulas: w proportional to S^-1(mu - g 1), g = 1'S^-1 mu / 1'S^-1 1
pitfalls: normalising to sum 1 when budget is 0

title: Turnover-penalised rebalance toward target weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: current drifted weights w0 [N], target w* [N], band or turnover cap tau, or penalty kappa. DITANYAKAN: rebalanced weights obeying band/cap. RUMUS: Partial: w=w0+s(w*-w0), s=min(1, tau/sum|w*-w0|); band: trade only names with |w*-w0|>b, back to edge or target per text. JAWAB: 1) compute deviation. 2) apply rule. 3) do NOT renormalise if the shrink is meant to leave gross<1 (card pitfall). 4) report turnover.
formulas: w = w0 + s (w* - w0), s = min(1, tau / sum|w* - w0|)
pitfalls: normalising after a final turnover shrink

title: Covariance estimation choices and annualisation before allocation
deliverables: mu [N] and Sigma [N x N] annualised
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1 x N] or returns, frequency P, return type, estimator (sample, EWMA lambda). DITANYAKAN: returns, mu and Sigma in annual units. RUMUS: Card V1/V2: ddof=1, arithmetic mu x P, S x P; EWMA S_t=lambda S_{t-1}+(1-lambda) r r'. JAWAB: 1) prices -> simple pct_change or log diff per text; drop first row. 2) estimator. 3) annualise. 4) check PD (eigvalsh>0).
formulas: S_t = lambda S_{t-1} + (1 - lambda) r_t r_t'

title: Kelly or MV backtest with rolling estimation and rebalancing
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N], window W, rebalance step, method (GMV, tangency, ERC, Kelly), constraints. DITANYAKAN: OOS weights and portfolio returns. RUMUS: Core 1-6 on trailing rows strictly before each rebalance; weights apply from next period. JAWAB: 1) for each rebalance date t use rows t-W..t-1. 2) estimate mu, S. 3) weights. 4) hold with drift until next date. 5) concatenate returns; summary stats. 6) check no look-ahead.
pitfalls: including date t in its own estimation window
